statement: After median or ulnar nerve repair, delay to repair, a more proximal injury level and older age are the strongest predictors of poor motor and sensory recovery; a substantial fraction of adults never regain useful function.

context.model: median and ulnar nerve transection and repair

measurement.assay: motor and sensory grading across pooled series
measurement.endpoint: recovery of motor and sensory function
measurement.effect: worse recovery with longer delay, more proximal level and higher age

replication.note: A meta-analysis pooling multiple independent series.

limitations: pooled retrospective series with heterogeneous outcome scales
predictors are associations, not a demonstrated mechanism

provenance.method: manual reasoning from the cited sources' abstracts (Crossref/Europe PMC), checked 2026-09-14; no source opened at figure level
